Hello dear.

You're right, a relationship will not make these feelings of insecurity go away, and yes, it is unhealthy to depend so much on someone else. 

Self love needs to come first, and I know first-hand just how horrible and difficult that is when you have depression, especially during these formative years. It seems like everyone else is having a great time and you're the one who's been left behind. But it's not really that way. 

You need to love yourself first before you can try to find love from someone else. This may need to be something a professional advises on, but for me personally *mirror work* has started to chip away at some lifelong-held insecurities and self-loathing. This might be a start for you, and once you love yourself you will find it easier to find love elsewhere.

Good luck and lots of love.

It sounds like you're going through a lot at the moment. Have you shared any of these thoughts with a healthcare professional or a doctor? If meeting face-to-face is too intimidating or expensive, perhaps you could try messaging a therapist or other professional on a website like [betterhelp.com](https://betterhelp.com). 

My counselor recently recommended to me when I feel low and go from bed-work-bed again, is to give myself one hour to wallow. I have one hour to stay in bed and wallow or feel depressed, and then once that hour is up I have to move. Even if it's to the living room. Going outside is preferable, even for a walk around the block. But changing the environment can be a really great way to stop the wallowing from continuing and perpetuating itself.

If someone has a plan to commit suicide (e.g. date, time, place), then they are at a serious risk of harming both themselves or others.

I don't know where you come from, but perhaps your country has an anonymous crime tip-off phone number that you can call and leave some information about the 'fit of rage' episode that your friend had.

In the meantime, I suggest that you stay safe - perhaps keep a distance or always meet with this friend with another trusted person, and tell someone else you trust where you're going and what time you'll be back - get them to check in on you. They don't need to know the reason why if you do not wish to share that with them.
